Container.Name: ajazz-companion-bridge
Container.Overview:
Use an Ajazz AKP05E (or compatible Mirabox) LCD button pad that is plugged into this Unraid server as a control surface for Bitfocus Companion. The bridge reads the pad over USB, talks to Companion through its Satellite API, shows Companion's button pictures on the pad and sends key presses, touch-strip taps, swipes and dial turns back. It reconnects by itself if the pad is unplugged or Companion restarts.
SETUP: (1) In Companion enable Settings > Satellite API (port 16622) and switch off Settings > Surfaces > "Enable connected Mirabox Stream Dock devices". (2) Set "Companion host" below to the IP of the machine running Companion. (3) Set "USB HID device" below to the pad's /dev/hidrawN node. The pad appears as two hidraw entries; you need the one whose HID_PHYS ends in /input0. In the Unraid terminal run: for d in /sys/class/hidraw/hidraw*; do grep -q 00000300:00003004 $d/device/uevent && echo "$(basename $d) $(grep HID_PHYS $d/device/uevent)"; done (for other pads use their USB id). (4) If the container log says "No supported devices found", re-check the node, and as a last resort turn Privileged on (Edit, Advanced View) and try again.
Only the Ajazz AKP05E is verified on real hardware; other Ajazz/Mirabox pads are experimental. If the pad is plugged into another computer instead, run the bridge on that computer (see the project page).
Container.Requires: An Ajazz AKP05E (USB 0300:3004) or another supported Ajazz/Mirabox pad plugged into this server, and Bitfocus Companion 3.0 or newer with the Satellite API enabled (it can run on any machine on your network).
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: ajazz mirabox akp05 akp05e stream deck companion bitfocus satellite macro pad

Config.Name: Companion host
Config.Description: IP address or hostname of the machine running Bitfocus Companion (use the Unraid IP if Companion is another container on this server).

Config.Name: Companion port
Config.Description: Companion Satellite API port (Settings > Satellite API in Companion).

Config.Name: USB HID device
Config.Description: The pad's /dev/hidrawN node: of the two hidraw entries the pad creates, the one whose HID_PHYS ends in /input0 (see the Overview for the command). The number can change after a reboot or replug.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: error, warn, info or debug. Use debug when asking for help.

Config.Name: USB write delay (ms)
Config.Description: Raise to 1, 2 or 5 if button pictures look torn or half drawn.
